fields: (a spec block, as terms-sheet): h, intro, cols [term, ours, note], rows [{p, v, m, link, link_label, part}]. part (look-only): what the clause governs on the drawing: "scope" (default), "base", "ro", "panel", "valve" or "option". A tag sits beside a small part (the valve), never on it, so the lit part stays in view; no leader runs through the rack, its pump or the panel on its way to another part's tag. A value written "a · b" breaks into lines.
best_for: ClauseTabs shows commercial terms as page one of a proposal on a clipboard, with a numbered tab on each clause and a leader from every tab to what that clause governs on a small isometric PP package (look `clause-tabs`, a spec block).

block.intro: Every proposal opens with these terms, in this order. FAT and SAT are the factory and site acceptance tests.

rows.v: Page one: scope in one plain line · Price and its basis · Issue date, valid [proposal validity, days] · Lead time in weeks · Exclusions
rows.m: Ends with every departure from your specification and its reason, or a written "none"
Stated on page one of each proposal

rows.v: [delivery terms] · [lead time from order, weeks] · [lead time from drawing approval, weeks]
rows.m: Two clocks, stated separately: from your order and from approved drawings
Each payment tied to an event you can check: approved drawings, passed FAT, delivery, accepted SAT
Not from shipment. One warranty text in proposal, manual and contract

rows.v: [warranty periods: package, service work, consumables] · [warranty exclusions]
